The upper part of the circle is located inside the triangle and is shaded gray; the lower part of the circle extends beyond the base of the triangle and is a white region. The part of the triangle that does not belong to the circle is also white. Reasoning: The entire composite figure can be divided into three non-overlapping parts: the gray overlapping part, the white triangle-only part, and the white circle-only part. The problem gives that the gray part accounts for 45% of the area of the entire figure, and the white triangle part accounts for 40% of the area of the entire figure. Therefore the white circle-only part accounts for 100% - 45% - 40% = 15% of the area of the entire figure. The entire circle consists of the gray overlapping part and the white circle-only part, so the area of the circle accounts for 45% + 15% = 60% of the entire figure. The requested proportion of the white circle-only part to the area of the circle is 15% / 60% = 1/4 = 25%.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a union of two overlapping shapes: a triangle outline and a circle outline. The shaded grey region is their overlap, and the unshaded lower circular cap is the part of the circle outside the triangle. From the text, take the grey overlap as 45% of the entire union and the white triangle-only part as 40% of the entire union. Since the whole shape is partitioned into three disjoint regions—grey overlap, white triangle-only, and white circle-only—the white circle-only part is 100% - 45% - 40% = 15% of the entire union. The whole circle consists of the grey overlap plus the white circle-only part, so the circle is 45% + 15% = 60% of the union. Therefore the requested percent is 15/60 = 25%.
